target_customer: Brazilian land lot developers (loteadores) and real estate developers who sell lots on installment plans
problem: Lot developers sell on long installment plans and struggle to manage and collect receivables and to get working capital against them. Hent automated collections and lent against the receivables.
business_model: Receivables management software plus credit and receivables advances to developers (fintech take on lending)
product_category: Proptech fintech: receivables management and credit

founders.name: Leo Pinho
previous_startups: Kaplen (card receivables reconciliation, acquired by Itau in 2015)

founders.name: Thiago Diniz
founders.background_notes: YC page bio calls him a serial founder and engineer.

founders.name: David Aragao
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page by one search summary; Motonow detail from one search summary only.

technical_complexity.rationale: Boleto based billing integration, collections automation and receivables tracking used as collateral are standard fintech engineering with some regulatory and credit modelling difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Once developers run collections through the platform, switching is costly, and real time receivables data supports credit decisions. The model is copyable by banks but the niche is narrow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the lot developer wedge. B3 has a general real estate receivables platform. Hent was later acquired by Arke per a founder bio.

market_need_then: Brazilian lot developers depend on installment receivables and had limited access to bank credit. Press in 2020 and 2021 described fast growth as the real estate sector heated up.

branding.domain_note: Uses hent.com.br, a Brazilian country domain, not an exact .com.

identity.visual_style: Plain B2B fintech site for developers

brand_strength.rationale: Regional B2B niche brand with local press coverage; no sourced evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Hent was founded in Recife in 2019 by repeat founders with prior exits in receivables and ticketing, and it targeted lot developers who live off installment receivables. It raised a seed led by Canary in 2020 and a small Virgo Ventures round in 2021, and press reported rapid growth. A founder bio on the YC page says it was later acquired by Arke, but the date, price and terms are not public, and the company site still showed independent branding in 2023.
notes: Seed amount reported by search summary as over R$5 million (Canary led); no USD figure verified so amount is null. Virgo round R$500 thousand, date 2021-08 from a seedtable URL and Startupi article. CB Insights lists 1.26M USD across 4 rounds, unverified. Reports of R$10M, R$40M and R$200M raises are unconfirmed. Acquisition by Arke comes only from a YC founder bio; no press found. Latka claims bootstrapped, which conflicts and is disregarded. Aragao's founder role comes from one search summary. No dated competitors found for lot receivables in 2020.
